Pi shows it is working, and a path in a name is not a folder

Wortel 2026.37.2 · 2026-09-09

Pi finally shows it is working. Pi ships with its progress reporting switched off, so Wortel had to read its screen to tell working from waiting, and that reading failed in two ways. It never watched the session you had selected, on the theory that you could see for yourself, so the one place you actually watched Pi work showed nothing. And every message Pi draws is wrapped in terminal marks that made the core believe a command had just finished, which switched the spinner off mid-turn and, with it, the “finished, your move” dot that follows a turn. Both are fixed. The selected session is watched like any other, with your own typing, pasting, clicking and scrolling discounted so a long prompt never reads as the agent at work, and a finished-command signal that arrives while an agent is running is ignored, since the agent, not your shell, still has the terminal. Expect the spinner a few seconds after Enter: this is Wortel guessing from the screen, and it waits for two changed frames before it commits.

  • A slash in a generated name no longer makes a folder. Session names come from your first prompt or the agent’s own title, and both are full of paths. “Debug web/src build” was being read as a session called “src build” inside a new folder called “Debug web”. Generated names now use a look-alike slash that the sidebar does not treat as a folder separator, so the path still reads as a path. A slash you type into a name yourself still moves the session into that folder, as before.
  • Quitting an agent no longer raises a “Command finished” dot. The finished-command signal at an agent’s exit was being reported like any long shell command. It counts as the agent leaving, not as a command worth flagging.
  • This applies to every agent that reports nothing, so opencode, goose and aider gain the spinner in the selected session too. Agents that announce themselves, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, crush and Amp, are unchanged.

Sessions name themselves, and a folder is a directory

Wortel 2026.37.1 · 2026-09-08

A session is named after what you asked for, seconds after you ask. Until now a row was called after its directory until an agent’s turn ended and the on-device model got a look at the screen, and that look tended to produce two or three words about whatever happened to be scrolling past. Now the name comes from the conversation. Claude Code already titles its own conversation from your first prompt and puts that title in the terminal, so Wortel reads it back: the row says “Debug git panel display issues with worktrees” a few seconds after you press Enter, matches what Claude’s own session picker shows, and follows /rename. Every other agent gets the same thing a different way. Wortel owns the terminal, so while an agent has just launched it watches for the first real line you type, hands it to the on-device model, and names the row from that. No hooks, no config files, nothing leaves your Mac, and the name is set once and held: it changes only when a new conversation starts in that session. A name you type yourself is final and nothing automatic ever touches it again.

  • Worktree sessions are named for the task, with the branch underneath. A session opened on a branch used to be called after the branch and stay that way. It is now named like any other session, and the branch moves to a second line under the name, with the same glyph as the toolbar’s branch chip.
  • A cut-off name shows itself on hover. Agent names are longer than branch names, so more of them truncate. Hover one and the full name appears as a tooltip, only when it is actually cut off.
  • A folder is a directory. A sidebar folder used to be a label: “New Session in Wortel” filed the session under Wortel and started it wherever the selected session had last wandered, which looked exactly like it had worked. Folders now carry a directory, new sessions start in it, and the path shows on the folder header. Set it from the header’s menu, or press ⌘O to open a folder from disk and get a session in it, filed under the folder that already covers it or a new one named for it. ⌘N beside a worktree session opens in the project, not inside the worktree.
  • The Session menu moves where a Mac app keeps its main menu, before Edit, and is grouped: starting a shell, folder commands, acting on the selected session, moving between sessions, jumping to one. “New Section” is now “New Folder…”, which is what it always was. ⌥⌘N opens a session at home when you want out of the current folder.
  • The git panel takes a selection. ⌘-click toggles a row, ⇧-click takes a range, ⇧↑ and ⇧↓ do it from the keyboard, and ⌘A takes everything. Stage, unstage and discard act on the whole selection with one confirmation, and dragging a selected file into the terminal carries every selected path.
  • ⌃⌥⌘. brings Wortel to the front from any app, whether it was hidden, buried or minimised. It is a registered hot key, so it needs no Accessibility permission, and the same chord cmux uses, so if you run both, whichever registered first wins rather than a coin flip.
  • ⌘W lands on the row above. ⌘N files a new session right after the selected one, so ⌘N, do the thing, ⌘W now lands back where you started instead of one row further down.

Two crashes, and ⌘Z belongs to the terminal again

Wortel 2026.34.1 · 2026-08-17

Wortel could quit on ⌘Z, and the longer the window had been open the likelier it was. This one came in from a window that had been up for five days. Typing in the commit box was registering its undo steps against the window rather than against the box, and those steps outlived the box every time the panel closed or you moved to another session. Pressing ⌘Z afterwards, with the terminal focused and the commit box nowhere on screen, reached for a step whose editor was long gone, and the app went down on the spot. The commit box keeps its own undo now, so nothing accumulates on the window and there is nothing stale left to reach for.

  • ⌘Z goes to your shell again. The same bug had quietly taken the key: once you had typed a commit message, the Edit menu’s Undo claimed ⌘Z for itself, and the terminal’s own undo (clear the line you are typing) stopped happening. Undo inside the commit box works exactly as it did.
  • Closing the last session no longer crashes on the way out. The window was being freed the instant it closed, while the app was still holding on to it, so anything that ran in the gap could land in memory that had already gone. Updating the title to say no session is selected was enough to do it. It only ever surfaced once the window was gone, which is the least useful moment to hear about it.
